   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  CITY CLERK’S OFFICE

  MEMORANDUM

TO:  City Council Elections Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons
  (Vice Mayor Craig A. Corman/Councilmember Mary N. Wells)

FROM:  Huma Ahmed, City Clerk

DATE:  January 14, 2026
SUBJECT:  Request for the City Council Elections Ad Hoc Liaisons to:
  1. Review the City’s Voluntary Campaign Expenditure Limit and
  Contribution Maximum
  2. Review Candidate Statement Costs
  3. Funding for the June 2026 Municipal Election

ATTACHMENTS:  1. Beverly Hills Municipal Code (BHMC): Ordinance 23-O-2883

INTRODUCTION
The next Municipal Election for the City of Beverly Hills is scheduled for Tuesday, June 2,
2026. Per California Senate Bill (SB) 970 election dates have been revised to the following:
on a non-Presidential Primary year, elections will be in June and during a Presidential
Primary year, local elections will return to March.

In preparation for the upcoming City election in June 2026, staff requests direction on:

  • Review of the City’s Expenditure Ceiling Limit and Contribution Maximum
  • Candidate Statement Costs
  • Funding for the June 2026 Municipal Election

The City consolidates its elections with the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County
Clerk’s office (LA County). All cities who coordinate with LA County for their elections
provide payment for election services.

DISCUSSION
Voluntary Campaign Expenditure Limit / Campaign Contribution Maximum

At the October 17, 2023, City Council meeting, the Council approved with recommendations
from the Elections Ad Hoc at that time (Former Mayors/Councilmembers Julian A. Gold,
M.D. and Lili Bosse) to increase the City’s voluntary expenditure ceiling for elections from
$80,000 to $100,000. Also approved was an increase in the City’s voluntary contribution
limit from $450 to $500 per contributor/entity.

The Elections Ad Hoc liaisons at that time did not recommend a change to the amounts for
candidates who do not accept the City’s voluntary expenditure ceiling limit. The current
 policy is that if a candidate chooses to not accept the $100,000 voluntary campaign
spending limit, then the candidate may only accept contributions of $125 per person/entity.

The City’s current voluntary campaign expenditure limit and campaign contribution
maximum was approved by the City Council in 2023. (BHMC 1-8-3 Voluntary Contribution
and Campaign Expenditure Limits)

Per the California Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC) the current State contribution
limits are $5,900 per person/entity. State campaign contributions apply to any city when the
municipal agency does not have laws addressing contribution limits for candidates. The City
of Beverly Hills has approved regulations in place for election fundraising and expenditures.

Costs for elections, supplies, staffing, postage, etc. have increased. Example: postage for
First Class Mail (metered bulk) has increased by approximately 25% over the past three
years.

Staff seeks City Council liaison direction on whether the approved amounts shall remain the
same or be updated for the June 2026 Municipal Election. If there is an interest in updating
the Voluntary Campaign Expenditure Limit/ Campaign Contribution Maximum, then an
Ordinance will be presented to the City Council for formal approval.

Candidate Statements

The Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk’s office publishes the Official
Sample Ballots, inclusive of Candidate Statements to all registered voters. Jurisdictions can
also opt for an online/digital choice to publish statements on LA County’s website.
Candidate statements can be printed in their Sample Ballots in print and online.

Historically, Beverly Hills candidates have been provided with an option, that if they agree to
the City’s Voluntary Campaign Expenditure Limit and Campaign Contribution Maximum, the
City will cover the cost for their statements. Currently, the cost is $800 (English only) and
$1,600 (English/Spanish). The cost for online postings with Los Angeles County is
estimated at $279.60 per Candidate Statement.

It is requested that the City Council liaisons provide direction on whether the City shall
continue to pay for candidate statement costs, should the candidates agree to the Voluntary
Campaign Expenditure Limit and Campaign Contribution Maximum.

Election Funding

The current election funding in the City Clerk’s Office is insufficient to cover these costs.
Multiple scheduled and unscheduled elections have been held in the past few years, placing
increased strain on the election budget.

When the City coordinates elections with Los Angeles County, whether for regular municipal
elections or statewide elections, City facilities must be used as in-person voting locations.
These elections involve significant logistical costs and ongoing outreach efforts. Citywide
informational mailers are also distributed to keep the community informed, further
contributing to overall election-related expenses.

  2 of 3
 FISCAL IMPACT
Currently, each year, a total budget of $110,000 is allocated for this fund. This fiscal year,
the City hosted one unscheduled election for the November 4, 2025 Statewide Special
Election. The City Clerk’s Office election budget is currently $85,000. The City has a
municipal election scheduled for June 2026 prior to the end of FY 25-26. There are no carry
overs or ongoing funds provided to this fund unless requested to the City Council. The costs
for Candidate Statements are listed above. Additional funding for this election is requested.

  Item  Cost  Comments
LA County Elections Costs $150,000 (approx.)  The amount is an estimate
(Consolidated)  depending on the number of
  candidates/ballot measures for
  an election.
City mailers + postage  $45,000  Significant costs from postage.
Candidate Statements  $1,880 per candidate (approx.)  Sample number of candidates
  $9,400 (x 5 candidates)  (could be more or less).

Estimated Total  $204,400  Requesting: $210,000

RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended that the City Council Ad Hoc Liaisons provide direction on the City’s
Voluntary Campaign Expenditure Limit and Campaign Contribution Maximum, the
Candidate Statement Costs and Funding for the June 2026 Municipal Election.

   ORDINANCE NO. 23-0-2883

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF BEVERLY
  HILLS AMENDING  THE  BEVERLY HILLS
  MUNICIPAL  CODE  TO  INCREASE  THE
  CAMPAIGN  CONTRIBUTION  LIMIT  FOR
  CANDIDATES WHO ACCEPT THE VOLUNTARY
  EXPENDITURE CEILING FOR CITY ELECTIONS
  AND  TO  INCREASE  THE  VOLUNTARY
  EXPENDITURE CEILING FOR CITY ELECTIONS

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS DOES HEREBY
ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The City Council hereby amends and restates paragraph A of Section
1-8-3 (“CONTRIUBITON LIMITATIONS”) of Chapter 8 (“CITY ELECTION
CAMPAIGNS; CONTRIBUTION LIMITS, VOLUNTARY EXPENDITURE LIMIT
AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS”) of Title 1 (“GENERAL PROVISIONS”) of
the Beverly Hills Municipal Code to read as follows:
  “1-8-3: CONTRIBUTION LIMITATIONS:
  A. Limits On Contributions By Persons And Committees:
  1. Except as provided in this section and section 1-8-4 of this chapter, no person
or committee shall make to any candidate, including the controlled committee of such
candidate, a contribution in excess of one hundred twenty five dollars ($125.00) for any
single election at which the candidate is attempting to be, or is, on the ballot.
Additionally, no candidate or candidate’s controlled committee shall solicit or accept any
contribution that will cause the amount contributed by the contributor to the candidate or
the candidate’s controlled committee to exceed one hundred twenty five dollars ($125.00)
for any single election at which the candidate is attempting to be, or is, on the ballot.
  2. Notwithstanding subsection A. 1 of this section, if a candidate accepts the
voluntary expenditure ceiling established by section 1-8-4 of this chapter, no person or
committee shall make to any such candidate, including the controlled committee of such
candidate, a contribution in excess of five hundred dollars ($500.00) for any single
election at which the candidate is attempting to be, or is, on the ballot. Additionally, no
candidate or candidate’s controlled committee shall solicit or accept any contribution that
will cause the amount contributed by the contributor to the candidate or the candidate’s
controlled committee to exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00) for any single election at
which the candidate is attempting to be, or is, on the ballot.
  3. The City Council may, by resolution, adjust the contribution limit established
in this subsection A in October of every odd numbered year to reflect any increase or
decrease in the California consumer price index since the last such adjustment of the
contribution limit. Such adjustments shall be rounded to the nearest ten-dollar ($10.00)
amount.

   4. The limitations of this subsection A shall not apply to contributions of a
candidate’s personal funds to his or her controlled campaign committee on behalf of his
or her own candidacy, and shall apply to contributions from the candidate’s spouse.”
  Section 2. The City Council hereby amends and restates Subdivision A of section
1-8-4 (“ELECTION CAMPAIGNS; VOLUNTARY EXPENDITURE CEILING”) of
Chapter 8 (“CITY ELECTION CAMPAIGNS; CONTRIBUTION LIMITS,
VOLUNTARY EXPENDITURE LIMIT AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS”) of
Title 1 (“GENERAL PROVISIONS”) of the Beverly Hills Municipal Code to read as
follows:
  1-8-4. ELECTION CAMPAIGNS; VOLUNTARY EXPENDITURE CEILING
  “A. A voluntary expenditure ceiling is hereby established for each
  election for City elective office in the amount of one hundred thousand
  dollars ($100,000.00). As used in this section, the term “City elective
  office” shall mean the offices of members of the City Council and City
  Treasurer. This section shall not apply in recall elections.”
  Section 3. Severability. If any section, subsection, subdivision, sentence, clause,
phrase, or portion of this Ordinance or the application thereof to any person or place, is
for any reason held to be invalid or unconstitutional by the final decision of any court of
competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this Ordinance shall remain in full force and
effect.
  Section 4. Publication. The City Clerk shall cause this Ordinance to be published
at least once in a newspaper of general circulation published and circulated in the City
within fifteen (15) days after its passage in accordance with Section 36933 of the
Government Code, shall certify to the adoption of this Ordinance and shall cause this
Ordinance and the City Clerk’s certification, together with proof of publication, to be
entered in the Book of Ordinances of the Council of this City.
  Section 5. Effective Date. This Ordinance shall go into effect and be in full force
and effect at 12:01 a.m. on the thirty-first (3 1st) day after its ssage.
